It is sad that a department with a relatively small budget still manages to waste it, given the domestic pressures we face.”

a3949.speaker: Thembi Msane, EFF MP
a3949.speech: Said Pandor should retire, and someone much younger should lead the department.

a3971.speaker: USAID (statement on its website)
a3971.speech: Said on Tuesday that all direct hire personnel would be put on leave from Friday, apart from “designated personnel responsible for mission-critical functions, core leadership and specially designated programs”; said personnel posted overseas will be recalled from their postings within 30 days; said it would consider case-by-case exceptions and extensions based on “personal or family hardship, mobility or safety concerns, or other reasons” ; “For example, the Agency will consider exceptions based on the timing of dependents’ school term, personal or familial medical needs, pregnancy, and other reasons. Further guidance on how to request an exception will be forthcoming” ; “Thank you for your service.”

a3971.speaker: Congressional Research Service
a3971.speech: According to it, USAID employs more than 10,000 people, about two-thirds of whom are stationed overseas.

a3971.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3971.speech: Asked by a reporter on Tuesday if he was preparing to “wind down” the agency, said, “I think so.”

a3971.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a3971.speech: Confirmed on Monday that he was serving as acting administrator of USAID.

a3971.speaker: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX
a3971.speech: Has called USAID a “criminal organisation“, without substantiation, and claimed the agency is a “viper’s nest of radical-left Marxists who hate America”.

a4051.speaker: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and International Organization for Migration (IOM) (joint statement)
a4051.speech: The United Nations and more than 100 partners launched a 2025-26 Joint Response Plan to deal with the grave Rohingya refugee crisis and are requesting "934.5 million dollars (862 million euros) in its first year to reach approximately 1.48 million people, including Rohingya refugees and the host communities." ; "The Rohingya humanitarian crisis, now in its eighth year, continues to be largely ignored around the world, but the needs remain urgent."

a4051.speaker: United Nations
a4051.speech: warns that the lack of funds will further reduce food rations and make access to basic goods even harder, with "disastrous consequences for this highly vulnerable population"; this extreme situation could "force many people to resort to desperate measures, such as dangerous boat journeys" to reach other destinations.

a4051.speaker: United Nations
a4051.speech: further noted that more than half the refugee population in the camps is made up of women and girls, "who face a greater risk of gender-based violence and exploitation", and that a third of the refugees are aged between 10 and 24 and "without access to formal education, adequate vocational training and opportunities to gain independence, they are deprived of future prospects."

a4238.speaker: Dr Nekoua M’Po, departmental director of Health for Atacora-Donga
a4238.speech: Underlined the importance of the campaign by highlighting the disastrous consequences of trachoma on human health; estimates, in epidemiological terms, at 8 million the number of people who are blind or suffering from visual impairment because of this disease, and at 41 million the number of people affected by an active infection; indicated that its transmission occurs from child to child by direct contact with ocular or nasal secretions during play or when sharing a bed, or indirectly through dirty hands, by way of soiled linen or flies, so that maximum contamination occurs at pre-school age.

a4238.speaker: Dr Nekoua M’Po, departmental director of Health for Atacora-Donga
a4238.speech: Acknowledged that a mapping carried out in Benin by the National Programme for the Fight against Communicable Diseases in 2014 and 2015 showed prevalence levels exceeding 10% in the communes of Natitingou, Boukoumbé, Toucountouna and Banikoara, making these the priority communes for the launch of the fight against this disease; invited the populations to give a good welcome to the community relays who are to conduct the various interventions in the field under the supervision of the actors of the health system.

a4238.speaker: Gervais N’dah Sékou, former prefect of the departments of Atacora and Donga
a4238.speech: Invited the populations to give a good welcome to the community relays: “Sight is life” ; “What quality of life remains to a sighted human being who then comes to lose his sight? What pain does that cause his family and his community?” — questions that led him to call on local elected officials to raise the awareness of the populations so that the success on which the other rounds and the coverage of the other zones of the country will depend may be achieved at the end of this first experience.

a4238.speaker: Zamora Francisco, representative of USAID, and Edmond Gbèdo, representative of the Ministry of Health
a4238.speech: Said that, in order to fight trachoma, the World Health Organization (WHO) has developed a global strategy integrating several interventions consisting of surgery for those at risk of blindness at the trichiasis stage, antibiotic therapy (TDM), facial cleanliness, and improvement of conditions of hygiene and sanitation — a strategy which in Benin benefits from the support of American partners, particularly the organisations ITI, RTI/ENVISION and USAID, through the National Programme for the Fight against Communicable Diseases.

a4239.speaker: Hamada Keiji, Japanese Ambassador to Mozambique
a4239.speech: Has pledged that the Japanese government will continue to provide support to the victims of Islamist terrorism in the northern Mozambican province of Cabo Delgado; speaking to reporters on Tuesday after an audience granted by Margarida Talapa, chairperson of the Assembly of the Republic, said the Japanese government will continue supporting the displaced people who are victims of terrorism, and added that assistance will also be provided to the Mozambican Defence and Security Forces (FDS): “I spoke to the Chairperson of the Assembly about our cooperation activities in Cabo Delgado province, because we have two pillars: the first is humanitarian assistance, through the United Nations agencies, and the second is cooperation for stability in that province, through the (Mozambican) Ministry of the Interior”

a4239.speaker: Hamada Keiji, Japanese Ambassador to Mozambique
a4239.speech: Said Japan is interested in stopping terrorism in Cabo Delgado, therefore it has been following the efforts the Mozambican government has been making to maintain stability and security: “We also want this stability because it’s not just for the Mozambican people who live in this province, but also for the liquefied natural gas extraction project, because there is a Japanese company that belongs to a consortium led by the French company TotalEnergies” ; “The Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) project in Area 1 of the Rovuma basin in Cabo Delgado, estimated at more than 20 billion dollars, is not just for Mozambicans, but also for the Japanese people” ; “So, in this case, I hope that the force majeure will be lifted, as soon as possible”

a4239.speaker: Hamada Keiji, Japanese Ambassador to Mozambique
a4239.speech: “We also talked about the future exchange between the Mozambican and Japanese parliaments” ; “This means that we may form a parliamentary friendship group. We have many parliamentarians who are interested in visiting Mozambique”

a4266.speaker: Dr Olasupo Olusi, Managing Director and CEO of the Bank of Industry (BoI) Limited
a4266.speech: Has said youth-led industrialisation, powered by innovation and entrepreneurship, can forge a pathway towards not only job creation but sustainable development and economic empowerment for the entire nation.

a4266.speaker: Dr Olasupo Olusi, Managing Director and CEO of the Bank of Industry (BoI) Limited
a4266.speech: Stated that the current state of Nigeria's industrialisation is woefully inadequate, with manufacturing contributing only 8.6% to the GDP, in stark contrast to much higher figures in countries like China (28%), Korea (25%), and Vietnam (23%) ; Painted a historical picture, indicating that despite previous efforts and policies aimed at stimulating industrial growth - like the National Industrial Revolution Plan (NIRP) and the Economic Recovery and Growth Plan (ERGP) - the pace of industrialization in Nigeria remains disappointingly slow, leaving Nigeria overly dependent on commodities, particularly oil.

a4266.speaker: Dr Olasupo Olusi, Managing Director and CEO of the Bank of Industry (BoI) Limited
a4266.speech: Highlighted Nigeria's demographic reality arguing that, "With a median age of just 18 years and over 70% of its population under 30, Nigeria is one of the youngest countries in the world. Yet, this youth bulge presents a dual-edged sword." ; "When a nation cannot absorb its youth into productive activity, the resulting frustration can lead to insecurity and disillusionment."

a4266.speaker: Dr Olasupo Olusi, Managing Director and CEO of the Bank of Industry (BoI) Limited
a4266.speech: Noted that as the oldest and largest development finance institution in Nigeria, BOI aims to serve not merely as a lender but as a catalyst for industrial growth and youth empowerment, citing the Youth Entrepreneurship Support (YES) Programme, the upcoming Industrial Innovation Fund to finance the full innovation lifecycle, and the BoI Impact Fund ; "I want to announce that in line with the current administration's Renewed Hope Agenda, BoI is supporting the Federal Government's drive to create a Youth Bank which will focus entirely on developing youth entrepreneurship."

a4266.speaker: Dr Olasupo Olusi, Managing Director and CEO of the Bank of Industry (BoI) Limited
a4266.speech: Articulated a vision for the future, where Nigeria could leapfrog into a modern industrial paradigm, embracing smart manufacturing and technology rather than simply replicating outdated models, and underscored the importance of a coherent strategy that integrates digital innovation and sustainability into the foundation of Nigeria's industrial policy.

a4266.speaker: Dr Olasupo Olusi, Managing Director and CEO of the Bank of Industry (BoI) Limited
a4266.speech: Cited numerous success stories of young innovators who have leveraged support from the Bank of Industry, including Blessing Ebere and Ibrahim Yusuf: "Despite limited support, these young entrepreneurs symbolise a wave of grassroots industrialisation" ; Emphasised that this entrepreneurial spirit could catalyse a broader industrial transformation for Nigeria, while highlighting that most youth-led businesses remain informal or small and are often disconnected from national industrial priorities due to structural barriers, and said intentional efforts must be made to create a conducive environment for entrepreneurship and innovation.

a4277.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a4277.speech: Announced on Monday on social media that more than 200,000 people will receive nearly 3,000 tonnes of food in the localities of Sake, Shasha and Bweremana, which recently came under M23 control ; the UN agency notes the intensification of fighting in the neighbouring province of South Kivu ; reported that since the capture of Goma by the rebels many of the nearly 300,000 people who had fled the fighting in Sake are beginning to return to their homes despite uncertain conditions.

a4277.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General
a4277.speech: Said that in total nearly 90,000 people have returned to the Karuba area, despite the lack of access to drinking water.

a4277.speaker: Ravina Shamdasani, spokesperson for the UN Human Rights Office
a4277.speech: Denounced the abductions of dozens of patients from hospitals in Goma by armed men, probably members of M23, stressing that the patients were accused of being Congolese soldiers or members of pro-government militias.

a4277.speaker: United Nations
a4277.speech: Reaffirmed that hospitals must be protected in all circumstances and that the wounded and sick must receive the necessary care.

a4277.speaker: Jean-Pierre Lacroix, head of UN peacekeeping operations
a4277.speech: Stressed, after meeting the provincial governor General Evariste Somo Kakule in Beni, the strong international convergence to support a resolution of the crisis in the east of the DRC.

a4308.speaker: Eldevina Materula, Minister of Culture and Tourism of Mozambique (message sent to the newsroom)
a4308.speech: Recognises the potential of Arão Litsuri as a contributor to the development of Mozambican culture through music and literature; extends heartfelt condolences to the family and to the makers of the arts; laments the passing of Arão Litsuri, who stood out in the world of the arts through his multifaceted personality, uprightness and great sense of building up Mozambican art.

a4308.speaker: FNB Moçambique (forecasts presented in Maputo)
a4308.speech: Forecasts that the Mozambican economy may grow 4.9% this year and 5.6% in 2025; although optimistic about the evolution of national GDP, the financial institution warns of possible risks arising from the political-military instability in the north of the country and the rise in commodity prices on the international market.

a4308.speaker: Police authorities (on the Beira road accident)
a4308.speech: Pointed to excessive speed and driver distraction on the road as some of the causes of the head-on collision involving a semi-collective passenger transport vehicle in Beira, which injured sixteen people, three seriously.

a4308.speaker: Ambassador of Brazil to Mozambique (during a visit to TVM)
a4308.speech: Made public the intention that Mozambique and Brazil strengthen cooperation in the area of Social Communication (media) and strengthen cultural relations between the two peoples.

a4308.speaker: Seminar on fundamental rights and gender-based violence, promoted in Maputo by the Ombudsman’s Office (Provedoria de Justiça)
a4308.speech: Recommended that the prevention of and response to gender-based violence should not be limited only to security and criminal justice institutions, but should be a responsibility of the whole of society.

a4368.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a4368.speech: Believes that private funding is a strategic imperative for sustainable development, as it is an engine of innovation, growth and value creation for Mozambique and other developing countries, and that leveraging companies and private investment is not an option but an essential condition for boosting Mozambique’s development in an accelerated and sustainable way ; “For this reason, we believe that private financing should seek to establish appropriate solutions, aimed, among other things, at stimulating the development of entrepreneurship, innovation, internationalization and company mobility.” ; gave the example of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which has 1.4 billion consumers, “a fact which will allow for a substantial increase in intra-African trade by 2045.” ; “That’s why governance and transparency, reform of the legal framework, promotion of local content and the development of innovative financing mechanisms are important to us. It is undeniable that public funding alone is insufficient to bridge the vast investment gap needed to achieve the country’s development goals.”

a4368.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a4368.speech: Explained that Mozambique’s national agenda consists of economic transformation, reducing poverty, creating decent jobs, especially for young people, and building resilient infrastructure, all in line with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals 2015-2030 ; “In addition to the significant structural challenges, the country’s development journey, like that of many developing countries, is ambitious and full of potential.”

a4368.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a4368.speech: According to the United Nations, development aid is currently facing a deficit of four billion dollars a year.

a4390.speaker: Federal Government of Somalia (statement)
a4390.speech: According to a statement issued by the Federal Government on Monday, the joint operations were carried out in Maqooqaha and surrounding villages, targeting areas where Al-Shabaab fighters had regrouped following recent offensives in June 2025 ; confirmed the elimination of high-ranking Al-Shabaab members, but did not disclose specific names of the leaders killed.

a4391.speaker: Tradeimex (Indian economic website)
a4391.speech: According to Tradeimex, the leading mango-exporting countries by value in 2023 were Mexico ($575.36 million, 30.08%), the Netherlands, Brazil, India, the United States, Germany and Burkina Faso ($27.63 million, 1.83%) ; also according to Tradeimex, the largest mango producers by volume are India (25 million tonnes), China, Indonesia, Pakistan, Mexico, Brazil, Malawi, Thailand, Bangladesh and Vietnam.

a4391.speaker: World Population Review (American specialist website)
a4391.speech: According to World Population Review, the main mango producers in Africa in 2021 were Malawi (1.7 million tonnes), Egypt, Nigeria, Mali, Kenya, Sudan, Tanzania, Madagascar, the DRC and Guinea ; and the main producers in the Arab world in 2021 were Egypt (1.3 million tonnes), Sudan, Yemen, Saudi Arabia, Oman, the UAE, Palestine, Somalia, Djibouti and Morocco.

a4391.speaker: Tunisie numerique (cited source)
a4391.speech: Cited as the source of the article.

a4470.speaker: Israel Katz, Israeli Defence Minister
a4470.speech: Says that the city of Gaza may be destroyed if Hamas does not accept the conditions imposed by Israel to bring an end to the war.

a4470.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a4470.speech: Announced that he will give final approval for the occupation of Gaza City and, at the same time, begin negotiations with Hamas to return the hostages and end the war.

a4470.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (data)
a4470.speech: Since 8 August, more than 50 residential structures have been attacked in the enclave's capital, causing the death of 87 Palestinians.

a4544.speaker: LHWC staffers (accusers, unnamed)
a4544.speech: Accused Secretary Helen Thandi Buluma of misconduct, including abuse of office and unethical behaviour.

a4544.speaker: Inside source close to the developments (anonymous)
a4544.speech: Told the Lesotho Times this week that LHWC staff are unsettled and demoralized, citing growing whispers of impropriety, abuse of office and unethical behaviour; said Ms Buluma's approach has created fear and division among staff, that her leadership relies on intimidation, punitive measures and retaliatory actions against dissenting voices, and that the suspension of three employees was a vindictive move. “Instead of inspiring trust, her presence at the helm fuels suspicion, division, and fear.”

a4544.speaker: Another source (anonymous)
a4544.speech: Said disgruntled staffers have escalated their concerns to the Lesotho government's Chief of Staff, Sofonea Shale. “This matter is serious, so much that it has been escalated to the Chief of Staff. The victims went to his office. It seems that she (Ms Buluma) is on probation, she has not yet been confirmed, but it is surprising that she seems to be problematic.”

a4544.speaker: Helen Thandi Buluma, Secretary of the Lesotho Highlands Water Commission (LHWC)
a4544.speech: Rubbished the claims, saying some staff members are resisting her efforts to follow laid down procedures to avoid financial mismanagement and procurement missteps; maintained the suspensions were necessary to protect the Commission's operations and ensure accountability. “They (suspended three) are the ones who know the systems . . . it is also important to protect them because they could be accused of tampering with the system. We asked them to step aside.” ; “We used section 17.5 — suspension from duty and criminal prosecution . . . We are not saying that they did this initially. We brought external IT auditors to investigate what happened and asked them to step aside.” ; “Section 17.5.2 says the suspension shall not be used as a form of disciplinary action. So, it is not a disciplinary action; it is a precautionary measure. Section 17.5.3 says employees suspended pending an enquiry shall be paid their full salaries and benefits for the period of such suspension.”

a4544.speaker: Helen Thandi Buluma, Secretary of the Lesotho Highlands Water Commission (LHWC)
a4544.speech: Described her arrival and management approach: “When I arrived, I received a very good reception. It is my first time in Lesotho, my first time working for a bi-national institution. I have worked for the United Nations, for parastatals in my own country, and in different countries. Compared with other places I have worked, the reception here was super. I had to take time to understand what was wrong in the office. From June, I understood we had to start enforcing the policies that are here. In a nutshell, it was relaxed, very relaxed compared to where I come from. There were a lot of policies that were not being followed ranging from procurement, finance management, governance frameworks. My role after three months was to ensure that we started following the policies that were already there. I didn't bring change. There was resistance, yes, but the majority worked with me. It's been a gradual journey where I felt welcomed. The resistance is usual; expected in an institution where people are used to doing things differently and somebody else comes.”

a4544.speaker: Helen Thandi Buluma, Secretary of the Lesotho Highlands Water Commission (LHWC)
a4544.speech: Explained the allegations of lost records and IT mismanagement and the purpose of the audits: “We found that we have lost 30,000 records on the system that we keep from way back, which is very critical, but this was never reported. Over time I asked for progress on the records, but I would get false reports that everything is okay until later we would discover that there is a problem — one of our systems crashed. Because they have given us the wrong information from May to date, we did not accuse them immediately . . . we are still investigating.” ; “My role is to make sure that we have an independent audit. The Secretariat is audited annually by independent auditors. We have instituted a forensic audit, but it is yet to start. We are going to do a forensic audit, and an ICT Cybersecurity audit. These are not to target anybody but to provide me with an independent view from somebody who looks at it professionally. They will give us a report and we will know what the problem is and what to fix. Yes, mis-procurement has happened.” ; “When you look at the mismanagement, the financial mismanagement, the funds that we use here are contributed by the two governments. Each of these countries has Public Finance Management Acts, meaning we are supposed to be accountable. I don't think most people understand that this is taxpayers' money. When you procure, in my mind, every cent, every Loti must be accounted for.”

a4544.speaker: Helen Thandi Buluma, Secretary of the Lesotho Highlands Water Commission (LHWC)
a4544.speech: Said there was a series of unsettling incidents at her home, raising concerns about security and potential interference as she nears the end of her probation: “I have beefed up security at my house, but between the 29th of August and today, strange things have been happening. I found the gate, which is normally locked, open at midnight. As we speak, the systems and remotes are being changed. We have security personnel in place, but it feels as though they know the exact times we patrol. I am the only one with the remote. The other day, the security team called to say the gate was wide open. I thought perhaps I had pressed the remote twice. I even reported it to the Commission. I have a cleaning lady who comes once or twice a week. On Tuesday morning, she reported that the gate was open. I asked the security team, and they confirmed that when they left at 5am, the gate was closed. Today, I checked at 11:30pm before going to bed, and the gate was closed. Later, the cleaning lady came and again said the gate was open. An investigation is underway to determine who has been accessing the property. I also have security cameras, but they are not working properly. I reported this at the office, requesting someone to check the camera systems. I am not sure if these incidents are connected to the issues at work, but my past experiences make me cautious. It is possible that the forensic audits could uncover something significant, and that some people may not want this information to come out. It is also noteworthy that Friday marks the end of my probation, so perhaps some individuals do not want me to be confirmed. Who knows?”

a4544.speaker: Helen Thandi Buluma, Secretary of the Lesotho Highlands Water Commission (LHWC)
a4544.speech: Defended her time at Malawi's National Oil Company (NOCMA), saying she was only victimised for standing for what was right.

a4544.speaker: Sofonea Shale, Lesotho government Chief of Staff
a4544.speech: Confirmed he was aware of the ongoing tensions: “I don't have a report, it is just that I am aware of these issues relating to civil servants. It was raised to me, but I do not have enough information to comment on it. It is not a matter which I can confidently say I have on my desk and I intend to act on it. I know there are issues of discontent in the Commission.”

a4544.speaker: Masupha Sole, Lesotho's technical advisor in the Lesotho Highlands Water Commission (LHWC)
a4544.speech: Said he was not aware of the claims: “I can only comment or deal with the issue once it has been tabled before me.”

a4544.speaker: Office of the Ombudsman of Malawi (2022 ruling)
a4544.speech: Ruled in 2022 that Ms Buluma's appointment as Deputy Chief Executive Officer of NOCMA was “unlawful, irregular, unprocedural, and amounted to maladministration”; the investigation found the role was not advertised, bypassed the Board and was not part of NOCMA's established structure, and the Ombudsman ordered that her employment be nullified, her contract extension declared void, and that she should not receive terminal benefits or gratuities.

a4544.speaker: High Court of Malawi
a4544.speech: Dismissed her challenge to the Ombudsman's decision, upholding the illegality of her appointment.

a4588.speaker: Claver Gatete, UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a4588.speech: Declared that foreign aid is no longer a viable solution to meet Africa's growing development needs, and said in a statement published Thursday by the ECA that the continent's annual Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) financing gap has reached $1.3 trillion ; Said African leaders must implement structural reforms to increase domestic resource mobilisation, develop regional value chains and move away from exporting raw materials: "Aid will not close the gap. We must stop exporting raw materials and importing poverty" ; Called for more investment in manufacturing, green industries and youth-led enterprises, while stressing that more than 80% of African exports remain raw.

a4588.speaker: Claver Gatete, UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a4588.speech: Reiterated the ECA's support for the creation of an African credit rating agency, arguing that current international rating practices distort risk and restrict access to affordable capital ; Said it was imperative for African countries to develop blended finance mechanisms, issue local-currency bonds and digitise tax systems in order to improve efficiency and compliance.

a4588.speaker: Robinah Nabbanja, Prime Minister of Uganda
a4588.speech: Said the continent was "dangerously behind," but highlighted progress made in her country, notably the reduction of maternal mortality, progress on gender equality and increased national budget allocations linked to the SDGs ; "The Kampala Declaration is concrete," she said, adding: "We are proud to host this debate and to advance it in terms of implementation." She said that despite this, debt pressures, limited access to concessional financing and the high cost of capital continue to pose challenges to many African economies.

a4591.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a4591.speech: According to the UN, more than 60% of Sudanese now live below the poverty line, and no clear plan for economic recovery exists as long as the war persists.

a4591.speaker: Humanitarian organisations
a4591.speech: Have repeatedly warned that, without immediate intervention, Sudan could experience one of the worst health crises of the 21st century.

a4591.speaker: World Food Programme
a4591.speech: Warned that Sudan is on the brink of famine and that millions of people risk dying of hunger in the coming months.

a4591.speaker: Many experts
a4591.speech: Agree that to stop the war it is necessary to have: a lasting ceasefire through international mediation (UN, African Union, Arab League); direct dialogue between the Sudanese authorities and the RSF, possibly with civil society; strong international pressure, with sanctions against parties violating truces and an arms embargo; a fight against foreign interference, limiting the role of mercenaries and halting outside support (weapons, financing); the opening of humanitarian corridors and delivery of food and medicine, as well as increased support for refugees (more than 8 million displaced); and an inclusive political settlement, with the restoration of a civilian government and negotiations involving all regions (Darfur, South Kordofan, etc.).

a4651.speaker: Ministry of Justice of Liberia (MoJ)
a4651.speech: has requested the Supreme Court to halt the ongoing case involving former Finance Minister Samuel Tweah and his co-defendants in an economic sabotage case; in the writ, the ministry asked Justice Gbeisay to pause proceedings in the case while prosecutors figure out the way forward on Judge Blamo Dixon’s decision to grant the US$8 million property valuation bond posted by Patrick Coleman that was intended to prevent Tweah’s incarceration; the Ministry cited Dixon’s decision on the US$8 million property valuation bond as one of the reasons for the stay order.

a4651.speaker: Associate Justice Yarmie Quiqui Gbeisay, Chambers Justice of the Supreme Court of Liberia (written order)
a4651.speech: issued a stay on the Criminal Court ‘C’ proceedings, temporarily halting further actions in the case. “You are ordered to stay all further proceedings and or actions in the matter pending the outcome of a conference on Tuesday, December 10, 2024,” Justice Gbeisay’s order, through a written communication dated December 3, mandated.

a4651.speaker: Judge Blamo A. Dixon, Criminal Court ‘C’ (court record)
a4651.speech: had initially set a hearing for the following day; he initially dismissed an effort by prosecution to force him to reverse his earlier decision to grant Tweah the US$8 million property valuation bond; during the hearing in September 2024, Judge Dixon mandated the prosecution to turn over to the defense team all pieces of evidence in its possession to satisfy the requirements of notice of discovery.

a4651.speaker: Cllr. Arthur Johnson, defense lawyer
a4651.speech: has repeatedly described the delay as “an abuse of the due process rights of the defendants” ; argued that the prosecution’s actions amount to contempt and delay strategies, hindering the fair trial rights of the defendants ; argues that prosecution has refused and neglected to respect the Court’s order for discovery, arguing “this is contemptuous” ; argues that the prosecution is engaging in “delay and dilatory procedure tactics” ; “This evidence by two unmeritorious letters of excuse by the MoJ under the signature of the Montserrado County attorney, Cllr. Richards Scott” ; told the court that such excuses must be prevented at any hearing as provided under the Liberian law, that the law provides for prosecution to appear in court to argue its excuse in the presence of a judge and not dictate in a letter sent to the court, and that a party requesting a continuance cannot dictate the time and date for it ; “In the minds of the defense, this constitutes contempt because it attempts to signal that the prosecution is playing the role of a judge not a prosecution” ; said the request is flimsy and attempts to employ procedural delay tactics and complete disrespect to the court and to defeat the ends of Justice ; “This is an abuse of the due process rights of the defendants including Tweah” ; said it was the same prosecution that announced to the world and the Liberian jury by media and public sentiment that Tweah was escaping Justice and that there was an Interpol alert issued by the government against the defendant, but with all of these assertions the defendants are yet to be indicted ; “The only desire and intent of the Prosecution was to see Tweah disgraced and incarcerated as their way of Justice, but not to accord a speedy and fair trial under the laws of Liberia.”

a4651.speaker: The defense team
a4651.speech: has raised concerns about the prosecution’s handling of evidence and procedural tactics, accusing them of disrespecting court orders; the defense maintains that the prosecution’s motives are political and seek to discredit and imprison Tweah without a speedy and fair trial.

a4651.speaker: Samuel Tweah, former Finance Minister of Liberia
a4651.speech: has since termed the trial as “politically motivated.”

a4651.speaker: Court indictment document
a4651.speech: The court’s document alleges that, between September 8-21, 2023, from transfer instruction documents submitted to the LACC investigation by the CBL, the total amounts transferred to the operational accounts of the FIA by the CBL as per the instruction from the MFDP are L$1,055,152,540.00 and US$500,000.00; it alleges that Tweah, along with Cllr. Nyenati Tuan, then Acting Minister of Justice and Acting Chairman of the National Joint Security, Stanley Ford, former Financial Intelligence Agency (FIA) Director General, and D. Moses P. Cooper, former FIA Comptroller, did conspire, collude, facilitate and commit the crime of Economic Sabotage (fraud on the internal revenue of Liberia; misuse of public money, property or record; and theft and/or illegal disbursement and expenditure of public money).

a4688.speaker: Government of Malawi
a4688.speech: Has asked local non-governmental organisations (NGOs) operating in the country to begin seeking alternative sources of funding, saying excessive dependence on donors could lead many to collapse.

a4688.speaker: Jean Sendeza, Minister of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare
a4688.speech: Expressed concern that many organisations were affected following the USAid funding cut earlier this year, particularly those in the health sector ; “We have seen that some organisations in the pavilions we visited have started implementing alternative approaches to generate resources for their activities. This is the way forward because relying solely on donors will not get us anywhere” ; commended NGOs for complementing the government’s efforts in national development, particularly in sectors such as health and education.

a4688.speaker: NGO Regulatory Authority (Ngora) survey
a4688.speech: A recent survey revealed that approximately 25.2 percent of 151 organisations reported being directly affected by the aid cut.

a4688.speaker: Innocentia Ottober, Ngora Board Chairperson
a4688.speech: Said NGOs had contributed around K1 trillion to the country this year, of which K747 billion was received in foreign currency, mainly United States dollars, British pounds and euros ; “NGOs are making significant contributions to the country’s development and we are pleased that the government recognises this. However, we still need effective systems to track the foreign exchange entering the country, as this money supports various national development initiatives.”

a4688.speaker: Faith Kadzanja, Family Planning Association of Malawi (Fpam) Communications and Advocacy Officer
a4688.speech: Said the organisation would continue working with the government to ensure the country is on track to achieve Malawi 2063 ; “For us to reach the goals of Malawi 2063, the population must be healthy and sexual and reproductive health must not be neglected. We want Malawians to use modern contraception so we can better manage our population.”

a4845.speaker: Evalista Kalimbuka, Vice Chairperson for Zomba District Council
a4845.speech: Said GBV could be prevented if traditional leaders and faith leaders join hands to check the malpractice by condemning it and raising awareness among their subjects of the evils of GBV and its negative impact ; called on the leaders to refer perpetrators of GBV to police and civil society organisations for justice ; "This is the day we need to deeply reflect GBV, We need to take part to end GBV," she said.

a4845.speaker: Evalista Kalimbuka, Vice Chairperson for Zomba District Council
a4845.speech: Observed that there is also psychological torture that is in the form of GBV, saying this needs to be checked as most women and men suffer in silence.

a4845.speaker: Ruperth Kasendero, District Gender Officer in Zomba
a4845.speech: Said GBV that is related to sex comes in many forms and child marriages are one of them ; said property grabbing is another form of GBV that needs to be looked into before it goes out of hand in Zomba, observing that cases of property grabbing are becoming common in the district.

a4845.speaker: Ruperth Kasendero, District Gender Officer in Zomba
a4845.speech: Called for collective responsibility to end GBV as opposed to leaving the task of fighting against the vice to the Gender Office only ; said his office intends to facilitate mobile courts to allow people in the community to know the criminality of GBV and the sentences that are given to perpetrators.

a4845.speaker: Newton Sindo, Representative of Zomba-based Civil Society Organisations
a4845.speech: Said GBV affects development at the household level ; warned men who abandoned children with no support, saying such men needed to be brought before justice for leaving the responsibility to women on their own.

a4931.speaker: Abdel Fattah Al-Sissi, President of Egypt (official message delivered by Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty to Bola Tinubu)
a4931.speech: reaffirmed Cairo's commitment to deepening its strategic ties with Nigeria, at both the bilateral and continental levels ; Egypt reiterated its willingness to strengthen its relations with Nigeria.

a5091.speaker: Dr. Ibrahim Abdi Hadi, Director General of the National Institute of Statistics of Djibouti
a5091.speech: Highlighting the importance of collaboration and joint validation, insisted on the commitment of all participants to refine the products presented, and evoked the vision of equipping the country with a cutting-edge statistical information system capable of guiding future development strategies with precision and of helping all actors of economic and social life in decision-making, notably by making adequate and up-to-date information and indicators available.

a5091.speaker: Dr. Ibrahim Abdi Hadi, Director General of the National Institute of Statistics of Djibouti
a5091.speech: Recalled that the stated ambition of the National Strategy for the Development of Statistics 2018-2022 (SNDS-II) is to "build a National Statistical System with an operational legal and organisational framework (with a strong and stable central body), endowed with adequate resources and able to respond sustainably to the monitoring and evaluation needs of national development programmes, international agendas and other users."

a5092.speaker: Dr. Vamsi Krishna, managing director of Hetero Group of Companies
a5092.speech: "Hetero is pleased to partner with the Gates Foundation to create a pathway for the sustainable and affordable supply of lenacapavir. This collaboration reflects our commitment to ensuring access to innovative HIV medicines for patients in India and other low- and middle-income countries."

a5092.speaker: Unitaid, the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), and Wits RHI
a5092.speech: Announced new commitments with Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Ltd. (DRL), another Indian manufacturer, reinforcing efforts to build a competitive generics ecosystem.

a5092.speaker: Public health experts
a5092.speech: See lenacapavir for PrEP as a transformative option for people who face barriers to daily oral PrEP, including stigma, adherence challenges, and inconsistent access to medication.

a5092.speaker: Study on lenacapavir scale-up
a5092.speech: One study showed that scaling up access to affordable lenacapavir to just 4% of the population in high-burden countries could prevent up to 20% of new infections; modeling suggests that the introduction of lenacapavir has the potential to prevent significant numbers of HIV infections.

a5092.speaker: Trevor Mundel, president of global health at the Gates Foundation
a5092.speech: "Scientific advances like lenacapavir can help us end the HIV epidemic—if they are made accessible to people who can benefit from them the most. We are committed to ensuring that those at highest risk, who can least afford it, aren't left behind."

a5092.speaker: Bill Gates, Chair of the Gates Foundation
a5092.speech: Announced earlier this week the foundation's $912 million pledge to the Global Fund's 2026-2028 replenishment fundraising campaign, which aims to save 23 million lives from HIV, malaria, and tuberculosis between 2027 and 2029.

a5092.speaker: Bill Gates, Chair of the Gates Foundation
a5092.speech: Made a historic announcement earlier this year that he would give away virtually all of his wealth to the foundation to accelerate progress on saving and improving lives; he also announced the foundation would spend $200 billion over the next 20 years, working with its partners to make as much progress as possible toward three primary goals: end preventable deaths of moms and babies; ensure the next generation grows up without having to suffer from deadly infectious diseases; and lift millions of people out of poverty, putting them on a path to prosperity.

a5092.speaker: Kate Hampton, CEO of the Children's Investment Fund Foundation
a5092.speech: "The deals announced today on generics are a major step forward in ending the HIV epidemic. They build on full value-chain investments by CIFF and others to foster a competitive market so that access to lenacapavir is affordable and reliable for all those who need it."

a5207.speaker: National Assises (final report of the National Commission)
a5207.speech: The assises recommended a minimum transition period of five years, renewable according to security conditions, the refoundation programme and the agenda of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES); they also suggested the dissolution of political parties as well as the drafting of a new charter, and proposed the elevation of the Head of State to the rank of Army General.

a5207.speaker: Dr Mamoudou Harouna Djingarey, President of the National Commission for the National Assises
a5207.speech: “In my own name and on behalf of all the members of the National Commission responsible for the National Assises, it is my pleasure and honour to hand you the present document.”

a5207.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the CNSP and Head of State of Niger
a5207.speech: Reiterated his thanks to the President in charge of organising the proceedings, who steered the consultations expertly with the unfailing support of his team: “I express all my appreciation and gratitude to all those who, closely or from afar and in whatever manner, took part in this work, copies of which we are today receiving from the hands of the president of the National Commission who led the proceedings of the assises. Thank you, honourable sir! Thanks to all the people of Niger who accompanied and supported you. Let us bear in mind that this is no longer the time for resentment, for divisions, for sterile antagonism. Everything we do must be inscribed in the defence and the preservation of the interests of Niger. Niger, without which we would have no reason to exist, this Niger that we have a duty to defend at the cost of our lives. God willing, we shall succeed.”

a5207.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the CNSP and Head of State of Niger
a5207.speech: “I believe that this deadline was sufficient for those who could not take part in the debate to make their contributions because, as we say and will repeat, 'Labou Sanni no', 'Zancen Kassa ne', 'Hala ledi non'. The interests of Niger are above any grouping, any individualism and any clannishness. Niger must exist for particular interests to survive; let us work for the existence of our country, particularly in this difficult time in which we face insecurity. As we have always affirmed, it is our responsibility to put an end to this importation of insecurity into our Sahel so that it may henceforth be a space of prosperity for all the peoples who live there, rather than a space of insecurity. And insecurity means misery and needless loss of human life.”

a5207.speaker: Brigadier General Mohamed Toumba, Minister of State, Minister of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration of Niger
a5207.speech: Held that history will record that the population, through the National Commission charged with conducting the proceedings of the National Assises, marked the beginning of a new chapter for the country, thereby contributing, as the Head of State expressed in his opening address, “to laying solid foundations for a future of political stability and of economic and social progress for all” ; specified: “The analysis of the summary of the final report contains, among other things, the formulation of several recommendations by the participants in the National Assises arising from the diagnosis of the social, economic, cultural and political context of our country, in connection with the five themes that served as the basis of the assises' work; the proposal of the draft Charter of Refoundation which, once adopted, will serve as the fundamental law with constitutional force of our country; and the adoption of three resolutions relating to the adjustable five-year transition period, the elevation of Your Excellency to the rank of Army General, and finally the dissolution of political parties and the adoption of a new charter of political parties that takes into account the sociocultural realities of our country.”

a5273.speaker: Chris Brown, singer
a5273.speech: He reportedly retorted to the man that he would rather behave like a boxer than like a gay man.

a5273.speaker: The young man who was assaulted
a5273.speech: Said he wanted to file a complaint.

a5326.speaker: Clemence Kato, State Attorney
a5326.speech: Told the Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court that the investigation into the case of forging firearm ownership permits facing nine people, including six police officers, is in its final stages of completion; claimed that there are a few items they are finalising and therefore asked the court to give him two weeks so that they can complete the investigation.

a5326.speaker: Geofrey Mhini, Senior Resident Magistrate
a5326.speech: Agreed with the prosecution side and adjourned the case until September 25, 2025, when it will be mentioned, with the accused out on bail.

a5326.speaker: Charge sheet (court record)
a5326.speech: According to the charge sheet, the accused face a 2025 criminal case carrying 16 counts of forging firearm ownership permits, contrary to sections 333, 335A and 337 of the Penal Code, Chapter 16, as revised in 2019; the permits are alleged to have been issued between December 5, 2024 and April 4, 2025, bearing the names of Ahmed Ally, Ahmed Ahmed Sandrudin, Omary Abdallah, Robert Koka, Fathi Ally, Mohamed Salim, Suleman Mbewa, Mickdad Chakindo, Irfan Nafari, Gulam Abbas Najafi, Ismail Ismail, Salim Salim, Marwaan Habretsh, Maurice Kitiwe and Said Mohamed.

a5326.speaker: The nine accused
a5326.speech: Were first brought before the court on July 28, 2025 and had the charges read to them, which they denied; they are out on bail.

a5524.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a5524.speech: Warned: “Do not test us in the north” ; in a speech to the Knesset also said that the world “needs to unite to defeat” Hamas ; “This war is also your [the international community’s] war”, he stated in the same address, associating Hamas with the Nazi regime.

a5524.speaker: Israeli parliamentary spokesman (anonymous)
a5524.speech: Told Hebrew media that the interrupted parliamentary session would be resumed as soon as possible.

a5524.speaker: Israeli army
a5524.speech: Confirmed that the air-raid sirens, which normally announce the arrival of rockets launched from Gaza by Hamas, also sounded in central Israel and in Tel Aviv.

a5524.speaker: International news agencies (reports)
a5524.speech: According to reports from the international agencies, Palestinians in the Gaza Strip crowded today into hospitals and schools, looking for shelter and with little food and water.

a5524.speaker: Sameh Shoukry, Egypt’s Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5524.speech: Said that Israel “has not taken a position to open the crossing on the Gaza side”.

a5524.speaker: Gaza hospitals
a5524.speech: Warned that they are on the brink of collapse, with the emergency generators that keep machines such as ventilators and incubators running having less than a day’s fuel left; the hospital units also reported that their reserves of medicines are almost exhausted.

a5632.speaker: José Sambo, Councillor for Territorial Planning and Urbanisation of the Municipality of Matola
a5632.speech: Highlighted the importance of the Metrobus in improving the passenger transport system.

a5632.speaker: Maputo municipal authorities
a5632.speech: Declare themselves satisfied with the take from property and vehicle taxes, despite a collection shortfall of about thirty per cent against the slightly more than four thousand million meticais forecast for public expenditure in 2017.

a5632.speaker: Portuguese Consulate in Maputo
a5632.speech: Expects, with the new visa application centre in operation, to exceed the roughly nine thousand visas that were issued in 2017, thereby leaving Mozambicans and citizens of other nationalities resident in the country more comfortable in making trips to Portugal.

a5632.speaker: Jabula Zibia, Provincial Director of Agriculture and Food Security of Zambezia
a5632.speech: Assures that extension workers and quantities of insecticide have already been mobilised to combat the pest that has destroyed more than one thousand hectares of maize and rice.

a5795.speaker: Antonio Guillen Hidalgo, Spanish Ambassador to Mali
a5795.speech: Said that the Kingdom of Spain is present in Mali through several projects, notably in rural development, health, food security, youth training and access to drinking water, as well as support for women; for the Spanish diplomat, Mali is considered by Spain a priority country in its development aid, which is why the AECID budget has been doubled, as has aid to the Sahel countries, within the framework of the Spain-Africa strategy 2025-2028. “Since 2008, Spain has always remained committed, against all odds, alongside the Malian people. And we hope to continue writing the book of the history of our relations for many years to come.”

a5795.speaker: Antonio Guillen Hidalgo, Spanish Ambassador to Mali
a5795.speech: At the handover of a giant cheque of 3 million euros to the World Food Programme in support of the Food Security Commission (CSA): “I thank you for the opportunity to announce the Spanish government’s commitment to food security in the Sahel and in Mali in particular. I am also pleased to inform you that the Spanish Cooperation Agency has granted 3 million euros to the WFP in support of the CSA. In total, Spain’s projected humanitarian aid to Mali in 2025 will be approximately 7 million euros. With this contribution, Spain is helping to confront the food crisis at a time when the number of people in a situation of food insecurity is rising, particularly in the Sahel, in Africa. I hope the Spanish contribution will be a relief for the populations. Spain supports the CSA in its determination to fight extreme hunger in Mali. We are aware of the urgent and alarming situation the country faces. And we are very pleased to work with the Food Security Commission. So the results of our support are always visible and positive.” ; Before specifying that “Spanish Cooperation is also trying to make its contributions to improve the situation with the construction of irrigation infrastructure and with the approval of food support for internally displaced persons and migrants within the framework of other interventions”.

a5795.speaker: Antonio Guillen Hidalgo, Spanish Ambassador to Mali
a5795.speech: In handing over three architectural models to the Higher School of Engineering, Architecture and Urban Planning (Esiau), specified that the gesture forms part of the strengthening of relations between his country and Mali, but more particularly with Esiau, which he described as one of the best schools in Mali; he praised the work accomplished by the institution’s dynamic team led by its director general Abdoulaye Déyogo.

a5795.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a5795.speech: Welcomed the quality of bilateral relations between the two countries and Spain’s clear-sighted and constructive approach to the situation in Mali and the Sahel: “The government attaches particular importance to objectivity in cooperation with our partners so that relations are founded on the constitutional principles that guide public action in Mali. To that end, I recognise and appreciate the attachment of our two countries to respect for the national unity and territorial integrity of States. I also salute at its true value Spain’s respectful and clear-sighted approach to the situation in Mali and the Sahel. To return to the ties between Mali and Spain, I note with satisfaction our convergence of views on questions of strategic importance such as international peace and security, particularly the fight against terrorism including in the Sahel, as well as good governance.”

a5795.speaker: Redouwane Ag Mohamed Ali, Malian Minister-Commissioner for Food Security
a5795.speech: Said the generosity of the Kingdom of Spain towards Mali has never wavered and has just been demonstrated again with this donation of 3 million euros: “It is today an irrefutable reality that the Kingdom of Spain stands out as a reliable partner, always available to accompany Mali, particularly in difficult times. With this new funding, Spain reaffirms its commitment to accompany Mali in preserving its food sovereignty through strengthening the resilience capacity of vulnerable communities. This gesture of solidarity and friendship comes at just the right moment to support the vision of His Excellency Army General Assimi Goïta, who places food security at the top of national priorities and wants no Malian to be left behind.”

a5795.speaker: Ernest Urtasun, Spanish Minister of Culture
a5795.speech: The Spanish minister praised Mali’s participation in Mondiacult 2025; the two ministers agreed to meet again soon on the occasion of Mali Day in Madrid to discuss further the strengthening of the cultural bridge between their countries.

a5795.speaker: Mamou Daffé, Malian Minister of Culture, Handicrafts and Tourism
a5795.speech: Congratulated the Director-General of UNESCO on the quality of the organisation of Mondiacult 2025 in Barcelona.

a5795.speaker: Audrey Azoulay, Director-General of UNESCO
a5795.speech: According to Ms Azoulay, “Mali is a source of inspiration for her and for the world”; she expressed the wish to visit Timbuktu very soon on the occasion of the World Forum of Civilisations planned for December 2025.

a5886.speaker: Afrobarometer survey (report)
a5886.speech: Findings of a recent survey show that Malawians are struggling to access public health services, with 81 percent of respondents who visited public health facilities stating that they found no medicines and 62 percent of citizens who visited a public clinic or hospital in the past 12 months saying it was "difficult" or "very difficult" to access the services they needed; "Many others report high costs that prevented them from getting needed care [69 percent], absent medical personnel [50 percent] and facilities in poor condition [46 percent]"; only four percent of respondents said they had some form of medical aid coverage.

a5886.speaker: Matthews Ngwale, Chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Health
a5886.speech: Reacting to the findings in an interview yesterday, said the results are a true reflection of the situation on the ground; said Malawi has not achieved its target to construct 900 health posts while healthcare workers and medicines are also inadequate in public health facilities.

a5886.speaker: Matthews Ngwale, Chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Health
a5886.speech: Said the health sector relies heavily on donors, but the withdrawal of USAid support should compel government to implement the national health financing strategy which provides ways of scaling up domestic resource mobilisation: "We need to make sure that some of the drugs should be purchased by ourselves, otherwise depending on donors for our healthcare will not take us far."

a5886.speaker: Solomon Chomba, President of the Physician Assistants Union of Malawi
a5886.speech: Called on the government to introduce levies to finance the health sector; said the government could establish national health insurance for people that can afford it but impose levies on commodities that leave people at risk of non-communicable diseases to help cover financing gaps in the public health sector.

a5886.speaker: Hester Nyasulu, Amref Health Africa in Malawi country director
a5886.speech: Called on the government to introduce levies to finance the health sector; said people also need to be empowered to report their complaints to hospital ombudspersons so that some of the challenges are dealt with at community level.

a5886.speaker: Parliamentary Cluster Committee on Health
a5886.speech: Said in March that K138 billion was required for procurement of medicines and laboratory items, against the K63 billion allocated.

a5886.speaker: 2024 Annual Economic Report
a5886.speech: According to the report, 55 percent of the country's health expenditure comes from development partners while the government contributes 24 percent and the remaining 21 percent comprises health insurance and out-of-pocket expenditures.

a5917.speaker: Nasser Bourita, Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5917.speech: “The Kingdom of Morocco can only welcome this agreement. But at the same time, under the leadership of His Majesty King Mohammed VI, Chairman of the Al-Quds Committee, Morocco hopes, first and foremost, that this agreement will be implemented and respected by all parties.” ; Stressed the importance of this development, which he said is in line with King Mohammed VI's vision of peace, and reiterated Morocco's constant position on the urgent need to end the violence and prioritise the protection of civilians.

a5917.speaker: Nasser Bourita, Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5917.speech: “In many statements since the outbreak of the crisis, His Majesty has stressed that the urgent priority is to establish a ceasefire. His Majesty has also made clear in multiple declarations that this ceasefire must be permanent, monitorable and lead to a lasting path.” ; Stressed that the ceasefire could bring several crucial benefits, notably ending the killings and destruction, saving lives, and facilitating a greater flow of humanitarian aid badly needed by the Palestinian people; added it would protect civilians, notably through the release of prisoners and hostages, and ensure civilians do not “bear the cost of these aggressions”.

a5917.speaker: Nasser Bourita, Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5917.speech: Added that Morocco hopes the ceasefire agreement will lead to the reconstruction of Gaza and support displaced families, describing this as a “key element in giving credibility to this agreement”; expressed Rabat's hope that the ceasefire will open the way to a lasting peace process and reiterated King Mohammed VI's call for a two-State solution including an independent Palestinian State with East Jerusalem as its capital: “His Majesty King Mohammed VI has repeatedly reiterated that it is no longer viable to continue managing crises in the Middle East without addressing their root causes. It is not a matter of ceasing fire to end one crisis and then waiting for the next.” ; Explained that there is today an opportunity to build on this agreement and launch a political process for a permanent and comprehensive peace in the Middle East within a two-State framework.

a6008.speaker: Ousmane Sonko, Prime Minister of Senegal
a6008.speech: Revealed that a $500 million funding package from the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), known as the "Senegal Power Compact" and set to span five years, has been suspended ; in a statement broadcast by the news website Seneweb: "We cannot continue to rely on foreign aid. The day before yesterday, the new U.S. President announced a three-year suspension of all American development aid to poor countries, pending further review."

a6008.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6008.speech: Has threatened to cut funding in response to a new land expropriation law in South Africa ; "South Africa is seizing land and treating certain groups of people VERY BADLY," he declared.

a6008.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a6008.speech: Sharply refuted these claims, emphasizing that the legislation is a constitutional legal process designed to ensure equitable land access ; "We remain a constitutional democracy firmly anchored in the rule of law."

a6008.speaker: Dr. Christopher Nyanga
a6008.speech: Underscored the programme's (PEPFAR's) critical role in making Botswana one of the first nations to achieve UNAIDS' 95-95-95 targets.

a6008.speaker: Ministry of Health of Botswana
a6008.speech: Has assured that access to antiretroviral drugs remains unaffected, although several local organizations have already been instructed to halt operations.

a6008.speaker: Government of Botswana
a6008.speech: Is planning discussions with the U.S. embassy to sustain the affected services.

a6225.speaker: Dr Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a6225.speech: Said in his opening speech at the 42nd meeting of the Programme, Budget and Administration Committee of the WHO Executive Board on 14 May 2025 that the loss of US funding and the decline in official development assistance from some other countries is creating a salary gap of more than US$500 million for the coming two-year period (2026-2027) ; "The bitter truth is that we need to reduce salary spending by 25 percent. This does not mean that we will cut 25 percent of staff across the whole organisation." ; "But let us not deceive ourselves; we are saying goodbye to a large number of staff with experience, ability and a high level of dedication. This means careers are interrupted and lives disrupted." ; "We expect that most of the staff reductions will occur at headquarters, although regional offices will also be affected to varying degrees." ; "Regional offices are finalising their plans, which align with headquarters."

a6225.speaker: Dr Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a6225.speech: Said that to help staff during this difficult period they have established support systems and are focusing on assisting their mental health and wellbeing; and that the prioritisation exercise produced a new headquarters structure, announced the previous month, reducing senior leaders from 14 to 7 and departments from 76 to 34.

a6225.speaker: Health stakeholders in Tanzania
a6225.speech: Have said that the United States' withdrawal from WHO is a major blow to developing nations, including Tanzania and poor countries.

a6225.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a6225.speech: Said the matter was expected given the trend of contributions to WHO by member states, that the United States had long been the largest contributor, followed by China, European countries and Japan, and that the withdrawal has reduced the organisation's operations, so a decision was taken on how to work under the present conditions ; "The organisation will be able to run itself without depending on many contributions; it will be able to think of new sources of income to fund its activities without getting stuck." ; "We know people have lost jobs; I do not know how many Tanzanians were on the employment list and how many will have been affected by the job cuts. But there are also projects run by WHO that will be affected in one way or another, or will fail to deliver the projects and the expected results for the beneficiaries of that funding. There are effects, but to a large extent they have reduced operating costs."

a6225.speaker: Dr Egina Makwabe, Chairman of the Association of Private Health Facilities in Tanzania (Aphfta)
a6225.speech: Said the United States contributes 30 percent of WHO's budget ; "If you look at the vaccine side, at Gavi (the international organisation that produces vaccines), in that plan to provide vaccines to poor countries, the United States was the biggest contributor."

a6225.speaker: Government of Tanzania
a6225.speech: Has said it has sufficient stocks of medicines and vaccines but is coming up with new strategies.

a6225.speaker: Daudi Msasi, Chief Government Pharmacist of Tanzania
a6225.speech: "We have no problem with ARVs; our medicine situation is good and it takes us up to June 2026. When the (Health) Ministry's budget is read you will hear the Government's plans," he said when speaking to Mwananchi about the strategies in place.

a6225.speaker: US President Donald Trump (executive order of 20 January 2025)
a6225.speech: Said in the order that the United States would stop providing funds, assistance or US Government resources to WHO; ordered the recall and reassignment of US Government staff or contractors working in any capacity at WHO; and said the US Government would seek credible and transparent international partners to take over essential activities previously carried out by WHO.

a6225.speaker: US President Donald Trump
a6225.speech: Complained during his first term that WHO had failed to adopt urgently needed reforms and was unable to demonstrate independence from the inappropriate political influence of member states ; "WHO continues to demand unfairly onerous payments from the United States, out of proportion with the assessed payments of other countries. China, with a population of 1.4 billion, has 300 percent of the population of the United States, but contributes nearly 90 percent less to WHO."

a6225.speaker: US President Donald Trump
a6225.speech: Accused WHO of allowing Covid-19 to become uncontrollable and of ignoring the danger of the disease, which has caused the deaths of thousands of people worldwide; blamed China for trying to cover up the outbreak and accused WHO of failing to hold China accountable and of favouring China, part of the accusations stemming from WHO's strong opposition to the US barring travellers from China, calling the disease the "China virus."

a6225.speaker: WHO statistics
a6225.speech: According to WHO figures, the United States provided Sh3.25 trillion in the period from 2022 to 2023; other major contributors in 2022-2023 were Germany (Sh2.16 trillion), the Gates Foundation (Sh2.10 trillion), Gavi (Sh1.21 trillion), the European Commission (Sh1.18 trillion), the United Kingdom and Northern Ireland (Sh1 trillion), Canada (Sh516.46 billion), Rotary International (Sh448.1 billion), Japan (Sh422.79 billion) and France (Sh407.6 billion).

a6283.speaker: Eshete Assfaw, State Minister of the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MoTI)
a6283.speech: Told Capital that under the government's plan, as of October 10 the country will fully stop oil import. “Until the end of September we will continue to import the product, and in this period local pressers will finalize their preparation with the direct support of the government” ; “Because of the current status we are confident that the import of final product will be fully suspended as of October 10.”

a6283.speaker: Eshete Assfaw, State Minister of the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MoTI)
a6283.speech: Reminded that the government conducted frequent meetings with potential big producers to commence their operation as soon as possible. “We have conducted several discussions and even directly visited the sites that are located in eastern Ethiopia and Amhara region,” he says, “we want to see a crucial shift on the sector.”

a6283.speaker: Eshete Assfaw, State Minister of the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MoTI)
a6283.speech: “Currently the country imports 40 million liters of edible oil every month, while in our evaluation local producers will commence operation as of August and some of them will commence operation until September” ; starting from August foreign currency that is now allocated for the import of final product will be shifted to producers, according to the State Minister.

a6283.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6283.speech: Said that the government is working to substitute the import of basic commodities like wheat and edible oil by local production. He said that the wheat production that expanded in these two years will enable the government to stop the import of wheat fully that consume close to a billion dollar every year. At the same time he said that the local oil producers that are at the final stage of the project will enable the country to replace the import by local production.

a6283.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a6283.speech: Told Capital that a few weeks ago the government has approved foreign currency for pressers to import crude oil.

a6383.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a6383.speech: Say Rubio's abrupt cancellation of his scheduled visit to Kenya is a direct response to Nairobi's warming relations with Beijing, growing corruption among top government officials, and Kenya's controversial ties with rebel groups in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Sudan.

a6383.speaker: State Department
a6383.speech: Announced that Rubio was expected to arrive in Nairobi on April 28 as part of his first diplomatic tour of Africa since his appointment by President Donald Trump in January, with the visit also set to include a stop in Ethiopia.

a6383.speaker: Officials in Washington (anonymous)
a6383.speech: Confirmed the trip has been called off at the eleventh hour, with no official reason given.

a6383.speaker: Hussein Mohamed, Kenyan State House spokesperson
a6383.speech: Described Ruto's visit to China as a continuation of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership established in 2017, highlighting Kenya's role as China's leading partner in the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) in Africa.

a6383.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
a6383.speech: During the visit to China, openly criticized Russia's invasion of Ukraine and, notably, condemned a recent U.S. vote at the UN Security Council that aligned with Russia.

a6383.speaker: Diplomats (anonymous)
a6383.speech: Have privately expressed frustration with the Ruto administration's regional posture.

a6383.speaker: Troy Fitrell, the State Department's top official for Africa
a6383.speech: Told reporters last week that U.S. diplomats on the continent have been instructed to prioritize support for American businesses and investment deals.

a6383.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a6383.speech: Indicate that several U.S. companies, which had previously committed to multi-billion-dollar investments in Nairobi, have now pulled out, citing Kenya's deteriorating corruption levels as a major deterrent.

a6383.speaker: Kenyan government
a6383.speech: Has yet to issue an official statement on the cancellation.

a6383.speaker: Steve Mbogo, prominent commentator on X (formerly Twitter)
a6383.speech: Wrote: "President Ruto chose the worst time to visit China-during heightened U.S.-China tensions over tariffs. Today, he's seen as a betrayer by his former ally, America."

a6383.speaker: Francis Mwangangi, Machakos Deputy Governor
a6383.speech: Told People's Daily that Secretary Rubio's cancellation likely stemmed from growing concerns over corruption and Kenya's engagement with rebel groups in the region.

a6394.speaker: Simon Robinson, Time magazine
a6394.speech: Had written of him, “The junior senator from Illinois, a man talked about as a future US President, is a celebrity in his father's homeland. His visit [in Kenya] has been front-page news for days, and at each stop crowds of hundreds, sometimes thousands, gather to cheer him, a stark contrast to South Africa, which he toured earlier in this trip and where most people have never heard the name Obama.”

a6394.speaker: Barack Obama, US Senator (Cape Town lecture, 2006)
a6394.speech: Described how his involvement in politics had evolved out of anti-Apartheid student activism in his university years. It was, he said, “the one issue that moved me for the first time in my life to become politically active and play a leadership role in my community. The issue was Apartheid. And as a young college student, I became deeply involved with the divestment movement in the United States… I tell this story, from time to time in the United States, to remind audiences that America simply has not been as exporter of a democracy and freedom. We have also been inspired by the struggles in other nations that have, in turn, helped shape and perfect the very freedom and rights held dear by citizens of my own country.”

a6394.speaker: Barack Obama, US President (2009 speech in Accra, Ghana)
a6394.speech: “I will focus on four areas that are critical to the future of Africa and the entire developing world: democracy; opportunity; health; and the peaceful resolution of conflict… Governments that respect the will of their own people are more prosperous, more stable, and more successful than governments that do not. With better governance, I have no doubt that Africa holds the promise of a broader base for prosperity… People must make responsible choices that prevent the spread of disease… promoting public health in their communities and countries. America will support these efforts through a comprehensive, global health strategy… Africa's diversity should be a source of strength, not a cause for division. We must stand up to inhumanity in our midst. It is never justifiable to target innocents in the name of ideology… I am speaking to the young people. You have the power to hold your leaders accountable, and to build institutions that serve the people…” ; “I can promise you this: America will be with you. As a partner. As a friend. Freedom is your inheritance. Now, it is your responsibility to build upon freedom's foundation.”

a6394.speaker: Barack Obama, US Senator (Cape Town, 2006)
a6394.speech: Had said that Africa's problems “thrive where corruption is rife and the majority of the population is impoverished and uneducated. And they can tear apart the social, economic, and political fabric of a region in a matter of days.”

a6394.speaker: White House (comprehensive strategy for Africa)
a6394.speech: Set out what is a fairly unexceptionable policy agenda of strengthening democratic institutions; spurring economic growth, trade, and investment; advancing peace and security in the region; and promoting individual opportunity and development.

a6394.speaker: The Guardian (UK)
a6394.speech: Explained, “There will be immense relief in South Africa, the continent's biggest economy, where an Obama no-show would have been regarded as a snub and fed paranoia that its pre-eminence was in jeopardy.”

a6394.speaker: Lindiwe Zulu, international relations adviser to South African President Jacob Zuma
a6394.speech: Told the Guardian they would expect a visit “because if he doesn't, we won't forgive him for that!”

a6394.speaker: Koffi Kouakou, political commentator and Witwatersrand University academic
a6394.speech: Told the Guardian, “The Chinese are coming and the Americans are not taking this thing seriously. Even Britain is out of the game. They're not engaged because of problems at home and the Chinese are having a field day. He's totally neglecting Africa. There's not enough time to catch up. It's a strategic neglect that is going to be costing America big time.”

a6438.speaker: Embassy of Iran in Windhoek
a6438.speech: Says Iran and the United States are expected to sign a memorandum of understanding on Friday, following an agreement aimed at ending more than three months of conflict between the two countries.

a6438.speaker: Dr. Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila, Speaker of the Namibian National Assembly
a6438.speech: Has reiterated the call for greater global commitment to humanitarian assistance and the protection of human rights during the just-concluded Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly held in Geneva, Switzerland.

a6438.speaker: Dr. Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila, Speaker of the Namibian National Assembly
a6438.speech: Has reiterated Namibia's commitment to strengthening parliamentary cooperation with Cuba.

a6438.speaker: Lukas Muha, National Council Chairperson
a6438.speech: Has urged parliamentary leaders to reinforce their role in safeguarding international law and advancing multilateral cooperation.

a6438.speaker: Victoria Kauma, Vice-Chairperson of the Namibian National Council
a6438.speech: Emphasised the country's efforts on gender equality through initiatives like the National Gender Policy and the Rural Women Parliament, at the 149th Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Assembly in Geneva.

a6438.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services
a6438.speech: Says that although the World Health Organisation has declared the end of the COVID-19 pandemic as a global health emergency, and Namibia has seen a decline in the positive rate, the country will not ignore its existence.

a6674.speaker: Save the Children
a6674.speech: According to Save the Children, around 120,000 children have been forced to leave their homes: "Some children are today separated from their parents and find themselves in a desperate situation in isolated areas," the organization reports.

a6674.speaker: David Okoni, member of a Save the Children partner organization
a6674.speech: "The situation is disastrous. Parents have neither food nor drinking water for their children, and those wounded by gunfire still have no access to medical care, because the health personnel have also fled to save their lives" ; "around 5 in the morning, gunfire began to ring out in Minova, driving people to flee in all directions. Many found themselves stranded without shelter, forced to sleep in schools, out in the open, and even in a warehouse."

a6674.speaker: United Nations
