a6674.speech: According to the United Nations, some 113 people have been wounded and hospitalized in health facilities around Goma.

a6674.speaker: Greg Ramm, Director of Save the Children in the DRC
a6674.speech: Warns of the gravity of the situation: "Children are caught in the crossfire and time is running out for them. Humanitarian access to already vulnerable populations is blocked. We urge all parties involved in the conflict to prioritize the protection of civilians and to guarantee unrestricted humanitarian access" ; said it is urgent that the international community act: "This includes providing emergency aid to displaced people, supporting efforts to protect civilians and working towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict."

a6674.speaker: Save the Children
a6674.speech: Says it has been working in the DRC since 1994 to respond to the needs of populations affected by armed conflict; says that in Minova it provides food aid, protection services and educational support in partnership with local organizations, and implements health, nutrition, water and sanitation activities as part of a consortium project.

a6914.speaker: Shadiya Alimatou Assouman, Minister of Trade and Industry of Benin
a6914.speech: In her opening address stressed the importance of the initiative for the Beninese economy: "This workshop is a crucial step for our nation. AGOA is a historic economic and commercial opportunity put in place by the American government, which offers privileged access to international markets, particularly that of the United States, and it is an opportunity we must seize fully in order to strengthen our productive and competitive capacities," she declared ; affirmed the government's determination to support local firms in their export efforts, in the face of the weakness of the supply of exportable products and the inability to meet the requirements of the American market ; "With the courageous reforms undertaken to improve the business climate and the processing of raw materials, this trend will be reversed, with an increasingly marked and regular presence of high value-added, quality Beninese products on the American market," she assured.

a6914.speaker: Brian W. Shukan, Ambassador of the United States to Benin
a6914.speech: Encouraged Beninese companies to seize this opportunity: "For more than 20 years, AGOA has been the cornerstone of trade relations between the United States and Africa. This legislation allows thousands of African products to access the American market duty-free, thereby offering African countries the possibility of fostering their economic growth and development" ; reaffirmed the commitment of the United States to support Beninese companies by facilitating access to one of the largest consumer markets.

a7179.speaker: Sam Nujoma, Founding President of Namibia
a7179.speech: Has called on all Ethiopians to come together and cease all hostilities and find amicable solutions to sustainable peace in the East African country, in a statement released by his foundation. “It is in that spirit, mindful of the provision of Security Council resolution 2457 (2019), that I call on all belligerents in Ethiopia to immediately cease hostilities, ensure humanitarian access and create the conditions for the start of an Ethiopian-led political dialogue as the only pathway to a just and comprehensive peace,” said the 92-year-old former president ; He said the lack of meaningful dialogue between the protagonists is particularly disturbing to him and therefore called on all Ethiopians to come together and cease hostilities, and that dialogue remains the only reliable and sustainable avenue to peace ; “There is no military solution to the conflict and battlefield victory cannot guarantee political stability in Ethiopia. I, therefore, appeal to the leadership of all sides to halt their military offensives in order to allow an opportunity for dialogue” ; “The only solution to the continuing conflict and the broader un-ending political upheaval in Ethiopia is a genuine commitment to an all-inclusive national dialogue that would chart an agreed pathway to a just and comprehensive peace.”

a7179.speaker: Sam Nujoma, Founding President of Namibia
a7179.speech: Called on the Panel of the Wise, the Forum For Former African Heads of State and Government (the African Forum) to support the mediation effort by the High Representative of the Chairperson of the African Union Commission, Olusegun Obasanjo ; He further called on all people of goodwill and leaders in Africa and the international community to continue to support the mediation efforts by Obasanjo.

a7179.speaker: Sam Nujoma, Founding President of Namibia
a7179.speech: Called on the Peace and Security Council (PSC) for their urgent intervention to resolve and manage the prevailing conflict in Ethiopia. “I appeal to you to facilitate timely and efficient responses to resolve the crisis situations in Ethiopia. Africa cannot afford a nation at war with itself. History has proven that civil wars have large and significant aggregate impacts on macroeconomic indicators such as GDP and trade,” said the Founding Father ; In addition, Nujoma said that in addition to affecting trade, violence can drive large scale human displacement, which in turn can have destabilising regional and global impacts, and that the number of people running away from civil war violence is far larger than the number of fatalities globally ; He said the conflict is likely to be a protracted and destructive war with significant ramifications for Ethiopia.

a7179.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopian Prime Minister
a7179.speech: Sent troops into Tigray in response to what he called “rebel attacks on army camps” last November.

a7179.speaker: Ethiopian government
a7179.speech: Declared a nationwide state of emergency earlier this month and ordered Addis Ababa residents to prepare to defend their neighbourhoods amid fears that the TPLF were heading for the capital.

a7246.speaker: Reverend Billy Gama, Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) board chairperson
a7246.speech: Urged religious leaders to avoid imposing political parties or candidates on their congregants as the country prepares for the September 16 General Election: "The point is that the church comprises people of different political affiliations, so the moment a religious leader begins showing political favouritism, the church is in danger of being torn apart." ; while acknowledging that the clergy has a role to guide people on how to choose responsible leaders, said people's right to choose a leader should be respected at all times.

a7246.speaker: Ron Johnson, Logos University Chancellor
a7246.speech: Said the institution offers high quality trainings and has programmes tailored to drive successful enterprises: "Religious leaders should have business ventures to support themselves and in so doing, it also makes their responsibility easy and they set an example for their congregants."

a7246.speaker: David Molapo, President of I Can Leadership Institute Africa
a7246.speech: Shared insights on balancing religious leadership and entrepreneurship.

a7295.speaker: Estevão Pale, Mozambican Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy
a7295.speech: “The success of the Beira–Angola pipeline can serve as a reference for the development of other pipelines or regional energy infrastructure. At the national level, it will increase the traffic of the Port of Beira and the use of the fuel terminal, promoting its sustainability, as well as creating local employment opportunities in the construction, maintenance and operation of this infrastructure.”

a7295.speaker: Estevão Pale, Mozambican Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy
a7295.speech: “These agreements go beyond simple technical partnerships; they represent a joint vision of interdependence and shared progress. Mozambique thus reinforces its geostrategic position as an energy corridor of SADC, contributing to regional energy security and to the balance of our trade balance through the export of energy.”

a7295.speaker: Estevão Pale, Mozambican Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy
a7295.speech: “This agreement also covers mechanisms for facilitating the trade of fuels, the use and the development of fuel infrastructure, guaranteeing the reliable supply of petroleum derivatives,” stressed the Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy in his speech.

a7295.speaker: Kenya Londe, Zambia's High Commissioner to Mozambique
a7295.speech: Said that the infrastructure will bring development and conveniences to both parties. Moreover, Kenya Londe states that the materialization of the project will create jobs. “The memorandum of understanding will benefit Zambians and Mozambicans, since it will generate many local jobs, and also because energy is the main source of development. Above that, we all need energy in order to produce.”

a7300.speaker: Ukrainian source close to the matter (anonymous)
a7300.speech: Told AFP on Saturday 22 February that the Ukrainian president is "not ready" to sign an agreement with the United States giving them preferential access to the country's minerals ; "The president is not ready to accept the draft in its current form. We are still trying to make changes, and to do so constructively." ; "They want to extract 500 billion from us" ; "What kind of partnership is that? [...] And why we have to give 500 billion, there is no answer."

a7300.speaker: Mike Waltz, US National Security Adviser
a7300.speech: "President Zelensky is going to sign this deal, and you will see it in the very short term, and it is good for Ukraine," he insisted at a gathering of conservatives near Washington.

a7300.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a7300.speech: Angrily rejected the first American draft agreement, arguing that he could "not sell" his country; he did, however, leave the door open to American "investments."

a7300.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a7300.speech: Stated on 1 February that Ukraine had so far received only 75 of the 177 billion dollars of aid voted by the US Congress.

a7300.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7300.speech: Claims that the United States spent "350 billion dollars to get involved in a war that could not be won"; he wants to obtain from Ukraine the equivalent of 500 billion dollars in rare earths as compensation for American support to Kyiv.

a7300.speaker: IfW Kiel economic institute
a7300.speech: According to the institute, total American aid to Ukraine - financial, humanitarian and military - reached 114.2 billion euros (nearly 120 billion dollars at the current exchange rate) between the beginning of 2022 and the end of 2024, including 64 billion euros in military assistance.

a7381.speaker: Mozambican Health Ministry
a7381.speech: Expects to vaccinate 18 million children, under 10 years of age, against the type 2 variant of polio, as part of the continuing efforts to eradicate polio from Mozambique.

a7381.speaker: Ussene Isse, Mozambican Health Minister
a7381.speech: Launching the national campaign in Maputo on Monday, said he believed it is entirely possible to meet this target, which is in line with other recent health interventions; said polio is a highly contagious viral disease whose main victims are children, striking the central nervous system and often causing paralysis. ; "In the border areas we will have special teams who will prioritise permanent contact with the children who are circulating in those areas." ; Said 81,892 people have been mobilised for the campaign, including vaccinators, supervisors, coordinators, data typists, independent monitors and drivers; called on all citizens to cooperate so that no child is left unvaccinated, allowing vaccination teams to visit their homes or ensuring their children head to the nearest health unit or other vaccination site.

a7381.speaker: Mary Louise Eagleton, representative of the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a7381.speech: Reiterated UNICEF's support for the eradication of polio. ; "We want to guarantee that all children from all corners of the country have the same opportunity for access to health and dignity. By vaccinating against polio, we are also strengthening the primary health care systems." ; Added that UNICEF will continue to support community development through clear information, social mobilisation, and strengthening trust in the health services.

a7397.speaker: Richard Chimwendo Banda, Minister of Local Government
a7397.speech: Addressed the crowd of protesting vendors, assuring them that the government, through the Reserve Bank, would provide forex support to vendors; before he could finish speaking, some protesters began throwing stones, forcing government officials to flee.

a7397.speaker: Richard Chimwendo Banda, chairing the parliamentary session
a7397.speech: Requested a pause in proceedings to allow MPs to monitor the developments; the request, submitted by Deputy Speaker Madalitso Kazombo, was approved, postponing parliamentary discussions until the following day.

a7397.speaker: Sosten Gwengwe, Minister of Trade
a7397.speech: Announced that the government had revoked business licenses of traders — especially foreign-owned businesses — accused of inflating prices unfairly; assured that forex allocation would be given to kaunjika traders in organized groups to facilitate smoother operations; acknowledging the legitimacy of the vendors' concerns, outlined a plan to provide financial assistance to importers of essential goods such as cooking oil, sugar, bread, soap, and second-hand clothing; warned that businesses that had unjustifiably raised prices must restore them to the levels recorded in December last year; confirmed that meetings summoning business suppliers would take place within the next 24 hours.

a7397.speaker: Opposition Members of Parliament
a7397.speech: Are demanding that the matter be formally tabled for debate, criticizing the government's approach and pushing for a full parliamentary debate on the vendors' grievances.

a7397.speaker: Dr. George Chaponda, opposition leader
a7397.speech: Speaking to journalists, stressed that, according to parliamentary rules, public concerns of this magnitude must be discussed transparently.

a7502.speaker: UN-FAO
a7502.speech: over four-fifths of Egypt's farmland employs flood irrigation, according to the UN-FAO, the most wasteful type of irrigation there is.
